messages:
leo: FYI onboarding demo hit a weird pattern: page 1-2 fine, page 3 stalls ~12s then a huge burst of requests and multiple 429s. reproducible with dotnet-sdk v0.3.0 and sample-app v1.9.
tara: logs?
leo: pasted minimal trace: ```
2028-07-22T14:05:01Z INFO page=1 sent=40
2028-07-22T14:05:02Z INFO page=2 sent=40
2028-07-22T14:05:03Z WARN page=3 wait queued=96 limiter=adaptive avail=0
2028-07-22T14:05:15Z INFO page=3 drain -> send=96 -> 429 x30
```
leo: looks like client stopped sending for ~12s, queued up, then flooded in one big flush. JS/Go weren't seeing this.
oliver: dotnet batcher groups by tenantId+model only. code: `var key = "${opts.Tenant}:{opts.Model}";` cursor not included. if pagination workers hit same tenant they merge into same queue.
tara: that explains merge, but why the 12s stall? is there a timer gating flush?
oliver: yes, the dotnet batcher has an internal timer that uses `Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(FlushMs))` with flushMs default=1000 and with a bug: when queue length exceeds threshold we expect immediate flush, but there's a race where Interlocked.Exchange flags are not set before awaiting, so concurrent workers skip the immediate flush and await the delay. result: queue keeps growing until the timer resumes and all flush at once.
leo: ugh. so two parity issues: (1) batch key lacks cursor, (2) flush race causes batching storm.
qa-marta: can you repro in unit test? add deterministic timing tests so we don't get flaky CI.
oliver: yes, I wrote a small repro harness that spawns 8 page workers and asserts no single flush > 20 items. also added fix: ensure flush trigger uses `Task.Run` to schedule flush synchronously instead of stacking on the timer. patch snippet: ```csharp
if (queue.Count >= flushThreshold) {
  Task.Run(() => FlushAsync()); // schedule immediate flush 
} else {
  await Task.Delay(FlushMs);
  await FlushAsync();
}
```
tara: also include cursor in key when opts.Pagination != null: `var key = opts.Pagination?.Cursor is null ? baseKey : baseKey + "|cur:" + opts.Pagination.Cursor;`
ops-jin: for live mitigation, we pushed org-scoped override to reduce dotnet default concurrency to 3 for affected demo orgs and set SDK env `REDUX_BATCH_FLUSH_MS=50` which smoothed it but not ideal.
leo: noticed token refresh plays a role too: concurrent 401s kicked off simultaneous refreshes, then all retried immediately causing extra inflight. dotnet token refresh uses a lock but releases it before waiting for network, so multiple callers cascaded. switch to using a single `Lazy<Task<Token>>` per client to singleflight refresh.
oliver: snippet: ```csharp
private Lazy<Task<Token>> _refreshTask;
public Task<Token> RefreshAsync() => _refreshTask ??= new Lazy<Task<Token>>(() => DoRefreshAsync());
```
qa-marta: i'll add integration test that runs sample-app in CI harness with `--page-streams 4 --page-size 200` and asserts no flush spike and no >20 429s in 60s window.
devx-bot: created ticket DEVEX-721 "dotnet pagination batching + flush race" assigned to @oliver.
oliver: opened PR 1723 with tests + changelog entry. planning canary tomorrow.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: dev-cluster, image=dotnet-sdk:fix-batcher-1723, start=2028-07-23T09:00:00Z
ops-jin: will hold mitigation flag until canary passes.
tara: docs: update onboarding note: "dotnet SDK: enable pagination-aware batching or lower client concurrency for large imports" and add sample-app flag `--per-page-batches`.
leo: repro steps for QA: 1) checkout sample-app branch devex/paginator-dotnet 2) set env DOTNET_SDK_BATCH_FLUSH_MS=100 PAGE_STREAMS=4 PAGE_SIZE=200 3) run `dotnet run --project src/sample-app -- --use-dotnet-sdk` 4) watch for steady flushes, not big bursts.
qa-marta: I'll run stress tests and report back. thanks team. :thumbsup:
